B2: Programming

SL: 40 hours | HL: 42 hours

Unit Overview

In this unit, you learn how to program effectively to solve problems. This is the largest practical part of the course. You work with variables, strings, exceptions, debugging, data structures, control structures, algorithms and file processing.

Unit Objectives

What students are expected to know:

  • how to write and trace programs using different data types and variable scope
  • how to manipulate strings and substrings
  • how exception handling and debugging work
  • how to use arrays, lists, stacks and queues
  • how to use sequence, selection, iteration and modularization
  • how searching, sorting and recursion work
  • how to read from and write to text files

Unit Outcomes

What students are expected to be able to do:

  • construct and trace programs using variables and data types
  • construct programs that manipulate strings
  • describe exception-handling techniques and use debugging methods
  • compare and use different data structures
  • construct programs using sequence, selection, iteration and functions
  • construct and trace search, sort and recursive algorithms
  • construct code for file-processing operations

Subtopics

B2.1

Programming fundamentals — variables, data types, substrings, exceptions and debugging

 B2.2

Data structures — arrays, lists, stacks and queues

 B2.3

Programming constructs — sequence, selection, iteration and modularization

 B2.4

Programming algorithms — Big O, searching, sorting and recursion

 B2.5

File processing — opening, reading, writing, appending and closing text files
